title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 'troisième mouture' of Analysis situs (June 1986), Grothendieck builds an 'atelier' M from a set L of 'points' equipped with a disjointness relation ∥. An atelier is a structure (M, ≤, ≪, ≭), axiomatised by At 1 to At 7. Here ≤ is an order, ≪ a 'well-inside' relation and ≭ a compatibility relation. omb(X) (the 'ombre', or shadow) is the set of points x with x ≪ X. For X, Y one sets omb(L) = ∪_{Z ≤ X,Y} omb(Z), the shadow of the common lower bounds. X ≭ Y (compatible) means: whenever x ∈ omb(X) and y ∈ omb(Y) both lie outside omb(L), then x ∥ y.

This page finishes Lemma 5 (stated on p. 30): if X ≭ Y, X' ≤ X and Y' ≤ Y, then X' ≭ Y'. Take x ∈ omb(X') \ omb(L') and y ∈ omb(Y') \ omb(L'), where L' is the analogous object for X', Y'. We want x ∥ y.
- If x, y ∉ omb(L), this follows from X ≭ Y.
- Otherwise, say x ∈ omb(L). Then there is Z ≤ X, Y with x ≪ Z.
- ML 1 is a 'meet/interpolation' lemma: if A, B ≤ C and x ≪ A, B, there is S ≤ A, B with x ≪ S. Apply it to X', Z ≤ X. This gives S with x ≪ S ≤ X' and S ≤ Z ≤ Y, so x ∈ omb(Y).
- By ML 4 (if Y' ≤ Y, x ∈ omb(Y) \ omb(Y') and y ∈ omb(Y'), then x ∥ y), it suffices to show x ∉ omb(Y').
- Suppose x ∈ omb(Y'). Apply ML 1 to S, Y' ≤ Y: this gives T with x ≪ T ≤ S, Y'. Then T ≤ X', Y', so x ∈ omb(L'), a contradiction. Qed.

Grothendieck then notes what remains. At_M 5, At_M 6 and At_M 4 a) are already proven, so only At_M 4 needs proof. That would establish that (M, ≤, ≪, ≭_M) is an atelier, with F = the set of closed parts of M consisting of pairwise ≭_M-compatible elements. The next page reduces this to Lemma 6 and a corollary, and checks that the induced disjointness on L is the original ∥.

Role: this is a 'realisation' step. From a combinatorial set of points with disjointness, it constructs an abstract topological workshop (atelier). This is part of Grothendieck's attempt at an axiomatic, point-light foundation of tame topology / analysis situs.
errors: No mathematical error found. The step 'soit p.ex. x ∈ omb(L)' covers the remaining cases by symmetry. ML 4 is applied correctly, since it does not need any hypothesis on y beyond y ∈ omb(Y'). The argument relies on ML 1 and ML 4 as stated on earlier pages, which I cannot fully verify.
Notational slip: the line written 'x ∥ Y' must mean 'x ∥ y'.

ideas.what: Hereditary compatibility: compatibility of X, Y (disjointness of shadows off the shadow of common lower bounds) passes to smaller X' ≤ X, Y' ≤ Y.
ideas.modern_name: Downward closure of a coherence/consistency relation; compare consistency in event structures and coherence spaces
ideas.where_published: Only in the unpublished Analysis situs notes (cote 156), as far as I know

ideas.what: Shadow omb(X) = {x : x ≪ X}, with an interpolation/meet lemma ML 1 for ≪ relative to ≤.
ideas.modern_name: Way-below relation and 'ways-below' sets in continuous posets / abstract bases; interpolation property
ideas.where_published: Unpublished; tame topology is only alluded to in Esquisse d'un programme (1984)

ideas.what: Constructing an atelier from a set of points with a disjointness relation; the closed families F are sets of pairwise compatible elements.
ideas.modern_name: Clique/ideal completion (coherence-space cliques; ideal completion of an abstract basis)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 1986 'atelier' formalism has a striking structural parallel with domain theory and linear-logic semantics. It uses ≤ plus a well-inside relation ≪ with interpolation, shadows ↡X, and a binary compatibility relation with families of pairwise-compatible elements. These correspond to the way-below relation and Girard's coherence spaces / Winskel's event structures, developed independently at the same time. The literature on Grothendieck's tame topology does not seem to note this.
missed.quote: F = ens des parties fermées de M formées d'él. 2 à 2 compatibles pour ≭_M
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This could link Grothendieck's unfinished axiomatic analysis situs (point-light topology, stratified spaces) to the well-developed theory of continuous domains, locales and stably compact spaces. That would offer tools for completing his programme or reinterpreting it.

deep.surprise_reason: The page itself is a routine lemma verification inside an unpublished axiomatic construction. Its interest lies in the unpublished atelier framework and its unremarked resemblance to domain-theoretic and coherence-space structures.
transcription_corrections: 'Si x * y [?] soit p.ex.' is likely 'Sinon, soit p.ex. x ∈ omb(L)', i.e. the case where not both x, y ∉ omb(L).
On the previous page, 'x ∈ omb(X') ∩ omb(L')' should logically be 'x ∈ omb(X'), x ∉ omb(L')' (and likewise for y).
